description: Read migration statements and report what each one touches and what it costs. Names the statements that rewrite a table, the ones that scan every row while holding a lock, the ones that discard data irreversibly, and the renames that break every client still deployed with the old name the instant they commit. Reports tables and columns touched so a reviewer can see the reach of a migration without reading every statement. Pay 300000 atomic USDC on Base via exact x402. MCP does not pay; it provides a challenge handoff.

concurrent_index_builds.description: Whether index builds should be counted as non-blocking. Defaults to false, because the blocking form is the default spelling. Setting it records that choice in not_examined rather than silently trusting it.

migration.description: The migration statements, in the order they would run. SQL text, at most 262144 bytes and 2000 statements. CREATE TABLE, ALTER TABLE, CREATE and DROP INDEX, DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE, GRANT and REVOKE are read; anything else is listed in not_examined rather than guessed at. No database is contacted and no rows are read, so an arbitrary schema can be audited with no credential and no grant.

name: sql_migration_blast_radius

complete.description: Whether everything supplied was examined. False means part of it was not, which is a different problem from something that is wrong.

finding_count.description: The true total, even when the listing is bounded.

low_risk.description: True only when no rewrite, scan-under-lock, destructive statement or rename was found and every statement was read.

passed.description: The same verdict under the name shared across the caller-supplied families.

request_id.description: Delivery request identifier; also returned in x-foundry-request-id.

title: SQL Migration Blast Radius
